text.p: Foreign currency reserves of the Philippines will reach $10.45 billion by Tuesday after the country draws down money from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), central bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Monday.
"By tomorrow it (reserves) will go up by $710 million," he said in a television interview.
The money is part of just over $1 billion the IMF is making available to the Philippines to replenish reserves following the de facto devaluation of the peso on July 11.
Singson said reserves had fallen almost $2 billion in the defence of the peso before its effective devaluation, bringing them to about $9.7 billion.
He also noted the country had substantial amounts of dollars available to it through foreign currency depository units.
